## In the MRP

Δπ is the projected five-year average HICP (Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices) inflation of the country minus that of the euro area, using projections from the [International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd) World Economic Outlook or the [European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd). Common euro-area inflation cancels out of the model, so only the differential matters. The MRP uses min{0, Δπ}: a negative differential is debited in full (about 6.3 percentage points of GDP of borrowing capacity per 100 basis points at the reference calibration); a positive differential is not credited, because differentials in a currency union tend to reverse through competitiveness.

## In the DAP

C2-E covers projections that are unavailable or implausible, with a fallback Δπ = 0. C2-T covers stale projections, with red flags such as legislated wage rounds, administered-price resets, or tax changes with mechanical price effects. C2-A covers imperfect indexation, with red flags such as bracket creep or a high share of expenditure indexed by law; these effects go to fiscal capacity, not Δπ. C2-M covers the labour-cost versus consumer-price differential, with a red flag being a unit-labour-cost differential persistently above the HICP differential, which triggers the C1-A2 check. Not crediting a positive differential is a conservative design choice that the DAP does not assess.

### [Country Report](../document-types/country-report.qmd)

- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) reports HICP inflation data and projections to assess price stability and differentials for [Inflation Differential](../parameters/inflation-differential.qmd). <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>

- Inflation projections for [Inflation Differential](../parameters/inflation-differential.qmd) are based on the Commission Spring 2026 Forecast, reflecting energy price dynamics. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) reports rising HICP inflation in 2025 and a forecast for 2026 to assess [Inflation Differential](../parameters/inflation-differential.qmd). <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The document reports HICP inflation forecasts for 2026 and 2027. It does not provide a specific euro-area average inflation projection for direct differential calculation, but implies convergence toward the [European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd) target via the 2027 forecast. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- HICP inflation projections account for rising fuel and service prices, linked to geopolitical conflicts and domestic demand. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The report provides HICP inflation figures for the country and compares them to the EU average, noting the impact of energy prices. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The document reports headline HICP inflation and compares it with EU trends, providing inputs for the inflation differential parameter. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- Inflation projections are based on wage dynamics, administered prices, and energy costs. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The report discusses the projected five-year average HICP inflation, noting that inflation in Slovakia is expected to remain above the euro area average, widening the cumulated inflation differential. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 4">ⓘ</button>

### [Economic Survey](../document-types/economic-survey.qmd)

- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) uses its Economic Outlook database for short-term projections. Consumer price index (HICP) and core consumer prices are reported to assess inflation dynamics. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Belgium_2024-09-23, p. 26" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Belgium_2024-09-23, p. 26">ⓘ</button>
- Wage indexation has pressured core inflation and temporarily weighed on price competitiveness. Unit labour cost growth has impacted export performance. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Belgium_2024-09-23, p. 28-30" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Belgium_2024-09-23, p. 28-30">ⓘ</button>
- Consumer price index (Harmonised) figures are reported for 2023–2027 to assess inflation trends. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 29" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 29">ⓘ</button>
- Inflation projections account for mechanical price effects from expiring energy support measures. Energy inflation surged from -7.8% in December 2024 to +5.2% in January 2025 due to the end of the electricity price brake and reinstatement of levies. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 24" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 24">ⓘ</button>

- A temporary increase in inflation from price resets is a risk following euro adoption. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 11" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 11">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) reports Harmonised Consumer Price Index (HICP) and core inflation figures. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Estonia_2026-06-08, p. 10" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Estonia_2026-06-08, p. 10">ⓘ</button>
- Headline inflation is expected to rise to 4.1% in 2026 due to higher energy prices, and to 2.6% in 2027. Core inflation at constant tax rates decreased from 3.8% in 2024 to 3.4% in 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Estonia_2026-06-08, p. 11" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Estonia_2026-06-08, p. 11">ⓘ</button>

The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)'s debt-sustainability risk classification and fiscal rules are referenced as key constraints on Dutch fiscal policy. [oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 13; <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 3" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 3">ⓘ</button>8]
